shortDescription: AutoZone NYSE:AZO reported mixed results for the fiscal fourth quarter, having experienced some of the same challenges reported by rival Advance Auto Parts NYSE:AAP last month.“In spite of a difficult selling environment in the first eight weeks of our quarter, we remained committed to executing on…

“In spite of a difficult selling environment in the first eight weeks of our quarter, we remained committed to executing on our strategies to grow both our domestic and international businesses,” AutoZone CEO Phil Daniele said.

Same-store sales, which measure sales in stores that have been open for at least a year and is a more accurate measure of traffic, fell to just 1.6% in U.S. locations from +4.8% a year ago, missing expectations for a gain of +3.12%. For the entire company, comparable sales were up 2.7% versus +4.5% a year ago and less than +4.17% estimates.

The company’s profitability improved, however, but that was partially attributed to tariff refunds and a non-cash LIFO impact. This translated into earnings of $56.05 per share, up from $48.71 in the same quarter last year and $2.16 better than expected.
With the addition of 97 new U.S. stores and 78 new international locations, AutoZone

sales increased 5.6% to $6.59B but missed expectations by $110M. Driven by a 145 basis point impact from tariff refunds and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO impact, gross margin increased 182 basis points to 53.3% in the fiscal fourth quarter.
